text:
maya g.: rolled out prefetch + soft-evict to helix in canary (20% of traffic) about an hour ago.

jordan: nice! quick numbers?

maya g.: p50 token latency down 22% (from 94ms -> 73ms), p95 down 9%, p99 unchanged (+2ms). cost per tok estimate -11% on small gen workloads. batch hit rate up from 63% -> 78%.

lee: what's soft-evict mean here?

maya g.: we prefetch likely-next KV pages for long-context requests and use a soft-evict TTL for rarely-hit KV entries so the cache stays warm for similar sessions. avoids full rehydrate spikes.

jordan: clever. runbook/flags?

maya g.: flag helix.prefetch=true and helix.cache.eviction=soft-ttl-300. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/helix/merge/4021

deploy-bot: canary rollout started by maya g. — traffic: 20% -> 20% (stable) :gear:

maya g.: Observability: added a per-route breakdown on Console (Route: /v1/generate) — dashboards show token-level cost delta and microburst p95.

lee: any weird regressions?

maya g.: noticed 1.5% increase in memory churn on host with very long KV chains but within OOM guard. we've added an autoreclaim for >95th percentile chain lengths. tracking in #eng-oncall.

jordan: Cool. Can we schedule batcher tuning for small-request-heavy customers next week? Might push batch hit to 85%.

maya g.: yep, I'll open a follow-up canary for microbatcher params. TL;DR: big win for tail-costs on chat workloads. :tada:

lee: nice work! can we get a short blurb for all-hands tomorrow?

maya g.: adding to announce draft in #all-hands after we validate canary to 50% tomorrow.

jordan: ping me when it's at 50% — I'll run the cross-region bench.

maya g.: will do.
